TLDR: if you're a Star Wars fan that isn't triggered by playing as a female, and you're also not sick of the 'Ubisoft Open-World Game Design Formulaᵀᴹ', you will have a good time with Star Wars Outlaws.


Pros:
- Beautiful, detailed open-world planets to explore, each one conveys the Star Wars aesthetic wonderfully. The first planet (Toshara) is sci-fi African plains, then there's a smaller city map (Kijimi) set on a cold/snowy planet, Akiva is another (rain-forest themed, this time) large map with explorable settlements throughout, and finally we get what is easily the most believable video game rendition of Tatooine yet (it's huge, Mos Eisley is present and fully explorable). Toshara and Tatooine especially felt like real places to me, they're so well done.

- Loyalty system across four Syndicate factions: pick/choose certain jobs as to not upset the wrong people. 

- Space exploration around the orbit of each planet (Tatooine is explorable, but there's basically nothing there of note). Toshara, Kijimi and Akiva have unique space environments to explore (ship graveyard / Nebula / Asteroid Belt). 

- Strong visuals taking advantage of forward-looking Ray Tracing tech... though there are some caveats to this (see cons list). Excellent art design.

- Cute critter companion. Engaging (if unoriginal) story.

- They absolutely nailed the 'cantina sleaze' vibe they were going for (it's a small thing but I love how you can just lean against the bar and soak in the atmosphere of the various cantinas). The game has a bunch of varied environments, characters and references that fans of this franchise will get a kick out of.

- Lock-picking is a little rhythm mini-game and it took longer than normal for me to get bored of doing it.

- The Speeder is fun and makes open world exploration less tedious (some of these maps are huge). 

- Sabbac (in-universe card game) is awesome once you get the hang of it.

- Personally I like the main character design a lot. There are a bunch of cosmetic options for your character/critter/ship/speeder, too. If playing as a female is such a burden, go play the recent Jedi games (both of which are great imo).

- Command your sci-fi axalotl critter companion to attack/distract enemies, open doors, interact with items etc. I love Nix!

- The HDR implementation is good, lights and engine exhausts look suitably bright/hot. 


Meh:
- Most of the game design is ripped straight out of Ubisoft's basic formula with some Star Wars flavoured tweaks stapled on. Personally I haven't played that many Ubisoft games in recent years, but I imagine if you play every entry of Assassin's Creed or Far Cry you will find most everything here boring or familiar (especially if you're not a Star Wars fan... but if you're not a fan, honestly why are you even bothering with this game?). That said there are a few unique features that fit the theme/setting well, for example: trying to talk out of getting caught when in stealth, and cheating at Sabbac in various ways. For the most part it's competently designed, but there's very little 'new' here.

- Sometimes you get caught in stealth when it doesn't feel like you should. Other times you wonder how these NPCs didn't notice you wolf whistle and upper cut their buddy who is standing right next to them (for the most part the stealth is functional though).

- Kay has all the usual 'Video Game Protagonistᵀᴹ' abilities: press button to scan environment for interactables, grapple rope to climb/swing, ability to climb certain walls or yellow painted railings etc. If you've played Tomb Raider or Uncharted you've experienced all of this before. Certain routes or collectibles are locked behind Metroidvania style 'ability gates' (rock barriers only destroyable with a specific blaster upgrade etc) but the game is decent enough to mark these on the map if you don't have the required tool yet. One of these skills (a cutting tool that lets you pass certain metal fences) isn't awarded until very near the end of the game; I take issue with this kind of design when it's paced this poorly, as by the time you're granted the ability you're either sick of playing (or the game is effectively over). 

- Further to the above, personally I didn't find the space combat that engaging as too many essential abilities (dodge rolling etc) are - again - locked behind upgrade quests, and by the time these functions were unlockable I'd already explored/completed the space content. Without these upgrades the ship combat felt too simple/boring.

- Maybe I have dementia but certain things aren't explained well in-game and I had to use Google to find out what the fuck I was doing wrong. I didn't understand how to play Sabbac at all during the tutorial (I swear it doesn't tell you the matching cards have to be different colours!) and I didn't realise you could extend/shorten your grappling rope until I was two thirds of the way through the game (there are an on-screen prompts for this at specific grappling points, I just didn't notice it).

- Given the 'outlaws' theme of this game it would've benefitted from more 'morally grey' quests with difficult choices or 'unwinnaable' outcomes (where there is no 100% positive solution) ala Phantom Liberty from Cyberpunk 2077.


Cons:
- This is probably the buggiest game I've ever played on PC in terms of stability. I've honestly lost count of the amount of times the game crashed, though I will say it was mostly from reloading saves or fast travelling... I don't think the game likes certain save states, which is probably why it doesn't let you manually save inside certain areas (that otherwise create autosaves). Also, you'll notice downed enemies respawn when you have to reload saves within these areas, it's like the programming is unable to account for NPCs that aren't in a default state. The save states in this game are kinda dogshit and I ended up forcing myself to manually save every now and then to not lose progress. I don't think my rig is the issue (Ryzen 5900x, 32GB RAM, RTX 5080) as you'll notice the Steam discussion board is rife with players moaning about crashes.

- Ray Tracing and DLSS are awesome technologies but they come with caveats and their limitations are more noticeable here than in anything else I've played. There is noticeable instability in the lighting/shadows (which often have an unattractive swimming/warbling appearance) and I also found that certain effects were either bugged (for example the heat haze effects on radiators/cooking equipment, check it out when you reach the top of the stairs upon leaving the cantina on Kijimi) or sometimes outright missing (some laser effects, blaster fire, sparks etc) as they were probably lost in the temporal mush this tech relies on. It's possible something isn't right with the way this tech is implemented, which is a shame because the game can often look absolutely stunning. This was all noted at max settings!

- Some animations lack weight, just seem generally goofy/robotic, or in the worst cases are bugged. The first time you sneak behind a Storm Trooper and watch Kay knock-out a fully armoured man bare-handed you'll probably laugh! I wondered why they didn't just give her a taser initially, but it turns out that's an unlockable ability that enables you to KO elite enemies and droids. Fair enough - but why couldn't she have started off with a baton or something to make this less silly (bare-knuckled KOs against unarmoured enemies look fine imo). Climbing in general feels poor in this game as sometimes prompts don't appear (causing Kay to awkwardly rub against a wall instead of grabbing it) or the character jumps off in a random direction. Lip sync during cutscenes is not great, and lighting can flash or freak out during camera cuts.

[b]Think twice[/b] before you buy this, even on a significant discount. This game had(s) a lot of potential to fill a legitmate Star Wars RPG void that nobody has attempted, and despite all the carbonite(lol) copies they could have picked from, they chose to reinvent the wheel. This is your typical Ubisoft slop with a Star Wars skin and a very mild attempt - from both companies - at staying relevant.

Yes, it's a good game, although far from a 9/10, which is what the setting, the name, and Ubisoft's generally positive track record with major titles might have suggested. It's beautiful, creates a unique atmosphere (ultimately through audio and visuals), and when it does feel "realistic," it actually is. I got it on sale.

It's basically Assassin's Creed on alien planets, which is fun in itself if you're into that sort of thing. It works quite well, is more stealth than blunt combat, and as others have already noted, the protagonist has a punch that puts even Mike Tyson and Bud Spencer to shame. In that sense, the gameplay isn't anything new, has hardly any flaws, and offers the familiar range of actions. Since Force powers play almost no role here, these actions are more physical in nature and therefore limited.

Technically, it's okay; it rarely crashes, and sometimes the character or bike gets stuck in some glitch, but you're usually safe thanks to constant saving (automatic or manual). This surprises me, because that never happened in AC Odyssey, for example, and you realize that SWO's technology must come from the same corner as soon as you whistle for the scooter... 🤦‍♂️

The major drawback, in my opinion, is the story and the character herself. You need a considerable amount of "suspension of disbelief" to really get into the story. First of all, there simply doesn't seem to exist a compelling reason why Kay Wess is doing what she's doing – like in other Star Wars stories where you have to save the galaxy or fight the Templars in AC. It seems to me that she just takes her pet Nix out of boredom and decides to become a galaxy-wide wanted gangster instead of a local pickpocket. That Nix doesn't have a care tag is surprising to me anyway, but that's Disney for you…

Furthermore, it's just as “logical” that every criminal organization was simply waiting for someone to come along and carry out their orders as it is that the empire, despite its massive presence, is clueless as always.

You wouldn't guess that Kay is supposedly a young woman in her early to mid-twenties (?) from her looks, and due to a lack of continuity (the movie term), some of her dialogue and behavior come across like that of an inexperienced 20-year-old, while others resemble those of an older, hardened gangster, even though they occur consecutively within the same mission. It's just odd. Kay “always" introduces herself to NPCs seemingly and without being asked, but only when it would make sense in the dialogue or the story does she omit it – to give just one striking example. 

Besides and as the one red line through the complete Star Wars universe, most of the interactions happen in and at bars. That's neat somehow but completely unrealistic, as a crowd in a bar would make a perfect place for any cop to observe suspects, as is known from basically any criminal TV series, novel or documentary. 

Conclusion after 17 hours of relaxed gameplay: An opulent work that scores points for me with its AC gameplay, beautiful "stage design" and fitting sound, but loses massively due to the superficiality of the staging, the dialogue direction and the "script" in general, besides smaller technical problems.

[h1] This shouldn't have worked so well! [/h1]

[h2]TLDR:[/h2] The game combines elements from Shadow of the Tomb Raider, The Witcher 3 and Freelancer into a fun adventure that can easily entertain you for 30+ hours. If that sounds good to you, don't listen to the haters and give it a try.

I think this game just got too much hate for all the bugs upon release, the mismanaged marketing and because it's just cool to hate on both Star Wars and Ubisoft nowadays. Of course the game has flaws. I’d even say none of what it does is perfect by itself, but in combination you’ll get a unique experience that’s so much more than the sum of its parts.

[h2]Here's what you'll probably enjoy:[/h2]
[list]
[*] The gameplay mechanics are very solid when it comes to shooting, stealth and exploring. It feels like 90% Shadow of the Tomb Raider which I'd consider the perfect execution.
[*] Interacting with the environment through your pet Nix is unique and allows for many good moments in exploration and combat.
[*] The world is beautifully handcrafted and full of details. None of the procedurally generated slob you find in many open world games nowadays.
[*] The ability system is well implemented and organically grows with your playstyle. It doesn’t feel like an arbitrary skill tree built around artificial XP points.
[*] The gameplay variety is immense and the pacing serves it well. You’ll never have to fight, sneak, riddle or explore too much at once.
[*] The world and quest design remind me a lot of The Witcher 3 with all the things you can do on the side. This goes on beyond the main story and can easily double your playtime if you enjoy the ride. I probably put 10+ hours in just playing Sabacc and upping my game with better shift tokens and cheating abilities. There are also environmental riddles, speeder races and arcade machines if you need a break from the adventure.
[*] The spaceship action takes me back to good old Freelancer days, an itch that only Everspace 2 and Chorus have managed to scratch ever since.
[*] You have plenty options to fine tune difficulty, convenience and HUD settings (with one exception mentioned below).
[/list]

[h2]This you might not like:[/h2]
[list]
[*] The quippy Marvel-like humor rarely lands and you need to just roll with it. It messes with the otherwise great story and characters.
[*] The big syndicate reputation system that Ubisoft marketing focused so heavily on is a joke and wasted potential. There are no lasting consequences for your choices and the cartels don’t really interact with each other. I’d recommend just staying on “good” terms with every syndicate (which you can even buy with data cards) and ignoring it for the rest of the game.
[*] Progression mostly comes through your abilities, tools and upgrading ship and speeder. Outfits and charms don’t do much and in the end there are only 2 or 3 outfits that make sense anyway (fortunately there’s transmog to get something out of the many clothes).
[*]The riddles are quite easy and generally revolve around observing the environment. Only the secret Jet Kordo questline is a tougher nut to crack.
[*] Speeder controls are very direct and not fun in my opinion.
[*] Climbing controls are weird and feel a bit clunky with the subpar camera.
[*] Despite the many settings, you can’t disable the button prompt for mounting objects and climbing walls which is just dumb and immersion breaking. There are mods to disable this, but why is it even there in the first place?
[*] Judging by other reviews there are performance and optimization issues. I played via Geforce Now Ultimate and it crashed only twice in over 70+ hours. However, one of these crashes put me back 3 hours as the autosave didn't synchronize. So if you play via GFN, make sure to manually save every once in a while.
[/list]

For me, the good parts far outweigh the annoyances and I’m glad I gave it a try. General advice for every (non-service) game: Wait until it’s fully patched and all DLCs are released, then only check current “after the hype” or “x years later” reviews. You might regret skipping this gem now that it’s complete.

Star Wars Outlaws is Ubisoft and Massive Entertainment’s first major open-world Star Wars action-adventure, and it largely succeeds at delivering a vast, lived-in galaxy that feels both familiar and fresh for longtime fans. You play as the scoundrel Kay Vess, a non-Force-using protagonist whose journey across richly varied planets like Tatooine, Akiva, Kijimi, and Toshara mixes shooting, stealth, space travel, and exploration, all underpinned by a dynamic reputation system that affects how different criminal syndicates treat you. The world is dense with activities — from side missions and expert challenges to hull-down bounties and planet-spanning exploration — giving real freedom beyond the linear corridors typical of previous Star Wars action games.

Visually and thematically, Outlaws captures the spirit of the Star Wars universe with authentic environments, bustling cities, and cinematic setpieces that evoke the feel of living in a galaxy “far, far away.” However, unlike titles such as Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order or Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, which unfold as guided, narrative-driven adventures with predetermined levels and pacing, Outlaws’ open world offers freeform play — letting you roam, engage in side content, and tackle objectives in many orders and styles. This gives it a scale and sense of discovery that Jedi games hint at but never fully embrace, even though the pacing and combat can at times feel less refined or punchy compared to those more focused titles.

That open structure will delight players who want the Star Wars sandbox experience with speeder bikes, orbital travel, and branching choices, though it can also highlight some of the game’s flaws: repetitive mission design, occasional technical hitches, and stealth or traversal systems that don’t always live up to their potential. Still, for anyone yearning for something closer to a Star Wars world you can live in rather than just play through, Star Wars Outlaws represents a substantial and generally rewarding evolution of the franchise’s gameplay.

Okay, so I get why everyone loves GTA. The city is huge, there’s chaos literally everywhere, and stealing cars, dodging cops, blowing stuff up—it’s a thrill. Some of the jokes land, a few missions feel like a legit action movie, and when things go completely off the rails… yeah, it can be hilarious.

But let’s be real: after a while, it’s kind of exhausting. The story doesn’t really stick, the characters are basically walking stereotypes, and the missions? Drive here, shoot there, run from cops, repeat. The “freedom” everyone talks about? Mostly just running around doing random stuff, because the city doesn’t actually feel alive—it’s just… there. And the bugs. Oh god, the bugs. Cars flying, AI freaking out, stuff clipping through walls… it’s funny sometimes, but more often it’s just annoying.

GTA is fun, don’t get me wrong. It’s loud, chaotic, and a little addictive. But it’s also overhyped. At the end of the day, it’s flashy, messy, and all about the spectacle—not a game that actually feels polished or deep. Fun? Sure. Great? Nah.

Good for chaos and laughs, terrible if you want anything more.

Realizare maximă: Am deblocat toate cele 77 de realizări, ceea ce arată cât de mult mi-a plăcut să explorez fiecare colț al acestui univers.

Lumea deschisă: Los Santos rămâne un loc iconic pentru orice gamer, oferind o libertate de mișcare greu de egalat.

Ce lipsește (Nevoia critică de update-uri):

Grafică „Epică”: Deși se numește Enhanced, încă mai trebuie lucrat mult la grafică pentru a oferi acea senzație vizuală epică pe care o așteptăm în 2026.

Modernizare: Jocul se simte învechit în mecanicile sale de bază. Este nevoie de update-uri care să modernizeze interfața și modul în care interacționăm cu lumea.

Suport continuu: Nu este suficient să relansezi jocul; este nevoie de actualizări constante care să aducă funcții noi și să repare micile probleme care trădează vârsta motorului grafic.

Concluzie: Recomand jocul pentru poveste și pentru satisfacția uriașă de a-l termina la 100%, dar sper ca dezvoltatorii să nu se oprească aici. GTA V are nevoie de update-uri serioase pentru a rămâne relevant și spectacolul vizual pe care îl merită fan

I have 164 hours in this game. At this point GTA V is less a game and more a lifestyle choice.

The open world is still incredible — you can do missions, run businesses, grind money, customize cars, or completely forget your plans and spend an hour doing absolutely nothing productive. GTA Online has enough content to keep you busy for months if you enjoy progression, collecting vehicles, and optimizing everything.

That said, GTA Online will test your patience. The game explains almost nothing, throws 47 phone calls at you the moment you log in, and occasionally reminds you that griefers and modders exist. Some updates feel amazing, others feel like they were designed by an accountant.

Still, there’s a reason people keep coming back. No other game lets you casually rob a bank, buy a flying bike, manage a nightclub, and then argue with random players in a public lobby — all in one session.

If you like open-world chaos, long-term grinding, and can laugh at the nonsense instead of rage-quitting, GTA V is absolutely worth it. Just don’t expect peace. Ever.

If you are considering buying this game for the story mode, I would highly recommend doing so. GTA V offers an extremely well detailed and immersive map that you can sink endless hours into, that even still holds up today despite being over a decade old. The amount of attention to detail, within the map, the in-game media such as websites, movies, and shows, and story is insane. I have roughly a combined ~1500 hours on GTA V/Online and I still find little details that I had never seen before.

I am making this review more specifically for GTA Online. 
GTA Online has so, so many issues that you can't really blame just one thing that makes it unpleasant to play. 
For starters, Rockstar has made the Online so absurdly anti-consumer that it is comical. The economy for GTA Online is so broken, usually against the player. Cosmetics, guns, properties, and upgrades are so absurdly priced and inflated, like the Stun Gun, costs 375,000 dollars? Missions and activities give almost nothing, and even doing the literal best money making methods, such as complex hour-long heists, still require multiple hours of non-stop grinding just to afford one relatively useful/new vehicle, not even including upgrades, or other barriers like properties or property upgrades. Not to mention that a lot of missions are designed to literally bore the player, you're given the slowest van and are tasked with driving across the map, playing delivery driver. It makes playing the game feel like a chore instead of something to have fun in, you are just doing the same mind-numbing activities just to afford that newly released car or property. 
I understand that Rockstar needs some form of monetization for constantly updating the online, but it seems like Rockstar is intentionally and artificially hindering player progressions and mission quality just to push players to purchase Sharkcards, that give players in-game currency. But what is even worse than Sharkcards, is GTA+, GTA+ is the scummiest anti-consumer aspect of Online. GTA+ is a subscription service that literally pay-walls content and has FOMO aspects like in-game items only being available for a limited time through GTA+. It is so frustrating seeing something get leaked or teased just to realize its unobtainable without buying the subscription. Even QoL features are locked behind the subscription, not to mention that the game constantly advertises GTA+ in-game on your phone. 

Another extremely jarring and frustrating issue with GTA Online is how the community/player-base functions. Instead of getting on Online to play with other people, I find myself, and many others, to be in their own bubble in an invite only lobby just grinding or playing missions alone/with friends. There are multiple reasons for this, such as griefers for one, but the online just doesn't work well for playing missions with multiple people, despite for being a literal online game. Playing missions with others can be so broken it's infuriating, sometimes the mission won't let send an invite, sometimes the game will desync and boot everyone out, and even when you do complete a mission, most of the time it'll just put everyone into different sessions just for you to have to load back into the clouds just to be in the same session. Rockstar won't even bother to fix these because they are too busy patching cosmetic exploits that don't even hurt the game (Rockstar blacklisting content is a whole separate issue)... Because of these issues people just don't even bother doing their missions or heists with multiple people, why go through all of that trouble when you can grind by yourself? Remember this is an Online game.

Even if you are willing to put up with these issues good luck trying to make new friends/communicate on this game, with the removal of text chat you can't even talk to people without texting them one at a time through the phone, why? If the developers are so incompetent that they have to nuke a feature because of links being spammed, a solvable issue, then the game never stood a chance. Why go into public lobbies if everyone is a mute and can't communicate? Why play with randoms on an heist if you can't make a plan? Even if you want to just do some fun adversary/PvP modes good luck matchmaking, as the 'quick-join' 90% of the time just doesn't even work, so no one even bothers trying to play them at all. All of these issues causes everyone who just wants to make money stay away from public lobbies, so now your left with lobbies that are just a playground for griefers and modders, making the situation even worse. Also I find it amusing how the game now requires BattlEye, yet modders are still apparent and can make your game unplayable and can potentially get you suspended/banned, how fun. 

I would only recommend playing GTA Online if you don't mind putting up with a grind, and if you have a group of friends who are willing to play. A lot of the content is locked behind having multiple people, so you need to have people who you can communicate with and are willing to put up with the game's server/sync issues. With the right people GTA Online can be an absolute blast, messing around in free-mode, doing big heists with friends, community game-modes... just avoid public lobbies unless you are willing to enter a giant war with the occasional modder who nukes the lobby and can get you banned. 
I love what is good about GTA Online, I just hope GTA VI's is better...

Bought it again. Yes, I’m the problem.

Look, I’m 39, I live in Canada, and I’ve probably spent more time in Los Santos than I have in my own backyard over the last decade. With GTA VI finally dropping in a few months, I just wanted to see how the "Enhanced" version actually holds up on a modern rig before we all move to Vice City.

The Technical Side: The Ray Tracing is the only reason to actually buy this. The reflections on the cars and the way the neon hits the pavement at night finally makes the game look like it belongs in 2026. It’s running at a locked 60FPS in native 4K now, which—given how poorly the original PC port used to scale—is a nice change of pace. No more stuttering when you’re flying a Buzzard over downtown.

The loading times are basically non-existent now. I used to be able to go make a sandwich while the game loaded; now I barely have time to check my phone.

The Vibe: As a massive Alien nerd, I’ve spent way too many hours on Mount Chiliad staring at the sky. The updated draw distance and lighting actually make the "mystery hunting" feel less like a chore and more like a cinematic experience. No Xenomorphs, obviously, but the atmosphere is top-tier.

Verdict: It’s the same game we’ve played for 13 years, just finally polished to the point where it doesn't look "old" next to modern titles. It's a solid way to kill time until May.

If you’ve got a high-end card and want to see Los Santos at its peak, grab it on sale. If not, just wait for VI.

GTA V is Rockstar at its most unhinged. It’s a game about crime, ego, and capitalism, told through three protagonists who should never be allowed near each other—or society. Michael is a retired criminal having a midlife crisis, Franklin is the only sane person in the room, and Trevor is what happens when chaos gains consciousness.

Los Santos is massive, alive, and absurd. One minute you’re pulling off a cinematic heist with military precision, the next you’re crashing a jet into a mountain because you sneezed on the controller. The satire is sharp, loud, and occasionally uncomfortably accurate—like holding up a mirror and flipping you off at the same time.

Then there’s GTA Online, which is a completely different beast. Story mode is a crime drama; Online is a lawless fever dream. It’s a place where:

Flying bikes shoot rockets

Everyone is dressed like a nightclub owner or a clown

You log in to sell cargo and log out traumatized

GTA Online feels like being dropped into a server full of supervillains with Wi-Fi. One second you’re minding your business, the next you’re vaporized by a teenager on an Oppressor who has absolutely nothing to lose.

Together, they form the full GTA V experience: a polished, hilarious single-player story paired with an online mode that’s pure digital anarchy.

10/10 — come for the heists, stay because a flying motorcycle just ruined your life.

[h1] TLWR: Wide as the ocean, deep as a puddle. Bad writing. Fun to be had but wait for a deep discount. [/h1] 

Bad writing, Main story puts you in control of three pretty loathsome characters making it difficult to really root for any of them. This also goes for any side characters in both single player and online, aside from a very select few, most are very annoying. Which is disappointing because GTA has always been very good at creating if not characters you can root for, then characters that are at least enjoyable. The main story also tries (and fails) to make a point at sometimes, but then immediately re-negs on said point. For example: [spoiler] There is a mission where you need to torture/interrogate someone suspected to be a terrorist; there entire time two characters are going on about how 'torture tactics never work and someone will pretty much say anything you want for you to stop torturing them, leading to false positives. But throw that all out of the window because after all of that blabbing. It works! You get the right guy.[/spoiler] Most of the story is almost a carbon copy of the movie 'Heat' as well. They did that for GTAIV as well but it was really only just a handful of missions, not the whole damned game. I honestly think no-one working on this game played GTAIV or any of the earlier games and I think that is pretty evident in some of the opening missions, like when [spoiler] Johnny from GTA Lost and the Damned gets killed in the games opening act. In a very uncharacteristic way might I add. I hated Johnny in Lost and the Damned but even then, having him be a strung out meth head in a trailer park goes so far against his character in GTA IV that it's almost a fucking insult. Johnny hated meth, didn't want to sling it and saw it ruin people very close to him. It was kind of a huge part of that games story. [/spoiler] - not a huge deal but emphasizes my point in that these writers were hacks. 

Speaking of hacks! On we go to GTA Online:

While I like that there are certainly plenty for you to do in both single player and online, none of the distractions really seem to go anywhere. Within about 20, 30 minutes you're just recycling the same missions. 

Most of the fun to be had in this game is in GTA Online, however it's not really worth it. It really all depends on how much you like busy work, how much you're willing to deal with being grieved, and if you have likeable friends to play with. The phrase "but it's fun with friends..." isn't enough to save a game. Literally everything is more fun with friends.  The game punishes you for doing well, as well; If you earn too much money at one given time, it just wont give it to you which is just peachy. Especially if you're a 'Rockstar VIP' more often than not, your second spin of the daily casino wheel will get poached out of your hands because of this. 

Graphics are nice and hold up I guess, but Rockstar always makes humans look as ugly as possible. That, and graphics just aren't enough to prove a game is good. 

Controller support isn't great. Sometimes it will just shut off your controller mid mission, awesome. Especially with newly added content. There are also some pretty game breaking glitches. For instance: In GTA online there is a (very overused) mission type where you deliver goods by van, anytime you hit the brakes the back of the van lifts as tied to a string and you are pretty much helpless as you dangle in your van and get shot at. [b][u][i]This still happens 10 years after release.[/b][/u][/i]

After playing the hell out of GTA IV and it still, to this day being one of my favorite games of all time, GTA V disappointed me at release and continues to 10 years later. Everything is just 'meh.' Most of Rockstar's good writers left after RDR2 so I don't really have high hopes for GTAVI; less so after learning it takes place in Vice City. Vice City was a good game but I'd rather they try something new. Maybe make fun of themselves and have GTA return to London? Maybe change the formula a bit?

The game is occasionally fun, but mostly in spite of its own design. Once the early dopamine rush wears off, it repeatedly gets in its own way and undermines the overall experience. From my time with it — and while I didn’t complete every heist or mission — the pattern became pretty clear.

Bunkers are bonkers: a 15-minute supply run window feels unnecessarily restrictive and turns routine tasks into stress tests. The nightclub, on the other hand, is excellent — no complaints there. MC businesses are mostly fine, except the hotbox weed runs, which are more frustrating than fun.

My biggest issues are with the NPCs and traffic AI. Enemies are absurdly accurate and overly tanky, and the traffic behaves like a coordinated hive mind dedicated to sabotaging whatever fun you’re having. After nearly 200 hours, the returns on enjoyment feel sharply diminished — the fun still exists, but it’s increasingly rare, while the stress carries over even after logging off.

I’ll grab an Oppressor, cause some chaos just to say I did, and then move on to greener pastures. So long, Rockstar — you made it hard to love this one.

I returned to Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced thinking I knew this city by heart.
Los Santos disagreed.

This isn’t a reinvention.
It’s a reminder of how well this world was built in the first place — now sharpened, smoothed, and unapologetically confident.

Everything feels tighter.
Lighting hits harder.
Streets feel denser.
Nighttime finally looks like a place where bad decisions are born.

GTA V was always about contrast.
Sunshine and corruption.
Freedom and consequences.
Three protagonists pulling the same world in different moral directions.

Enhanced doesn’t change that — it amplifies it.

Michael is still trapped by comfort.
Franklin still wants more than the streets will allow.
Trevor is still chaos with a pulse.

What hits harder now is the pacing.
Switching characters feels instant.
Chases flow better.
Gunfights are cleaner, louder, more readable.

The city breathes more.
Crowds react faster.
Traffic feels angrier.
Los Santos doesn’t just exist — it pushes back.

Online content looms in the background, but the single-player experience still stands tall.
The writing hasn’t aged — it’s matured into satire that feels even sharper today.

• I drove aimlessly → the city told stories.
• I followed missions → the characters unraveled.
• I caused chaos → the game smiled and let me.

GTA V Enhanced doesn’t ask you to relearn anything.
It asks you to remember why this worked so well.

It’s still absurd.
Still cynical.
Still confident enough to let you fail loudly.

By the end, Los Santos didn’t feel new.
It felt permanent.

9/10 –
Not because it changed the game,
but because it proved how hard it is to outgrow it.

[h1] TLWR: Wide as the ocean, deep as a puddle. Bad writing. Fun to be had but wait for a deep discount. [/h1] 

Bad writing, Main story puts you in control of three pretty loathsome characters making it difficult to really root for any of them. This also goes for any side characters in both single player and online, aside from a very select few, most are very annoying. Which is disappointing because GTA has always been very good at creating if not characters you can root for, then characters that are at least enjoyable. The main story also tries (and fails) to make a point at sometimes, but then immediately re-negs on said point. For example: [spoiler] There is a mission where you need to torture/interrogate someone suspected to be a terrorist; there entire time two characters are going on about how 'torture tactics never work and someone will pretty much say anything you want for you to stop torturing them, leading to false positives. But throw that all out of the window because after all of that blabbing. It works! You get the right guy.[/spoiler] Most of the story is almost a carbon copy of the movie 'Heat' as well. They did that for GTAIV as well but it was really only just a handful of missions, not the whole damned game. I honestly think no-one working on this game played GTAIV or any of the earlier games and I think that is pretty evident in some of the opening missions, like when [spoiler] Johnny from GTA Lost and the Damned gets killed in the games opening act. In a very uncharacteristic way might I add. I hated Johnny in Lost and the Damned but even then, having him be a strung out meth head in a trailer park goes so far against his character in GTA IV that it's almost a fucking insult. Johnny hated meth, didn't want to sling it and saw it ruin people very close to him. It was kind of a huge part of that games story. [/spoiler] - not a huge deal but emphasizes my point in that these writers were hacks. 

Speaking of hacks! On we go to GTA Online:

While I like that there are certainly plenty for you to do in both single player and online, none of the distractions really seem to go anywhere. Within about 20, 30 minutes you're just recycling the same missions. 

Most of the fun to be had in this game is in GTA Online, however it's not really worth it. It really all depends on how much you like busy work, how much you're willing to deal with being grieved, and if you have likeable friends to play with. The phrase "but it's fun with friends..." isn't enough to save a game. Literally everything is more fun with friends.  The game punishes you for doing well, as well; If you earn too much money at one given time, it just wont give it to you which is just peachy. Especially if you're a 'Rockstar VIP' more often than not, your second spin of the daily casino wheel will get poached out of your hands because of this. 

Graphics are nice and hold up I guess, but Rockstar always makes humans look as ugly as possible. That, and graphics just aren't enough to prove a game is good. 

Controller support isn't great. Sometimes it will just shut off your controller mid mission, awesome. Especially with newly added content. There are also some pretty game breaking glitches. For instance: In GTA online there is a (very overused) mission type where you deliver goods by van, anytime you hit the brakes the back of the van lifts as tied to a string and you are pretty much helpless as you dangle in your van and get shot at. [b][u][i]This still happens 10 years after release.[/b][/u][/i]

After playing the hell out of GTA IV and it still, to this day being one of my favorite games of all time, GTA V disappointed me at release and continues to 10 years later. Everything is just 'meh.' Most of Rockstar's good writers left after RDR2 so I don't really have high hopes for GTAVI; less so after learning it takes place in Vice City. Vice City was a good game but I'd rather they try something new. Maybe make fun of themselves and have GTA return to London? Maybe change the formula a bit?

The game is occasionally fun, but mostly in spite of its own design. Once the early dopamine rush wears off, it repeatedly gets in its own way and undermines the overall experience. From my time with it — and while I didn’t complete every heist or mission — the pattern became pretty clear.

My biggest issues are with the NPCs and traffic AI. Enemies are absurdly accurate and overly tanky, and the traffic behaves like a coordinated hive mind dedicated to sabotaging whatever fun you’re having. After nearly 200 hours, the returns on enjoyment feel sharply diminished — the fun still exists, but it’s increasingly rare, while the stress carries over even after logging off.

I’ll grab an Oppressor, cause some chaos just to say I did, and then move on to greener pastures. So long, Rockstar — you made it hard to love this one.

I returned to Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced thinking I knew this city by heart.
Los Santos disagreed.

This isn’t a reinvention.
It’s a reminder of how well this world was built in the first place — now sharpened, smoothed, and unapologetically confident.

Everything feels tighter.
Lighting hits harder.
Streets feel denser.
Nighttime finally looks like a place where bad decisions are born.

GTA V was always about contrast.
Sunshine and corruption.
Freedom and consequences.
Three protagonists pulling the same world in different moral directions.

Enhanced doesn’t change that — it amplifies it.

Michael is still trapped by comfort.
Franklin still wants more than the streets will allow.
Trevor is still chaos with a pulse.

What hits harder now is the pacing.
Switching characters feels instant.
Chases flow better.
Gunfights are cleaner, louder, more readable.

The city breathes more.
Crowds react faster.
Traffic feels angrier.
Los Santos doesn’t just exist — it pushes back.

Online content looms in the background, but the single-player experience still stands tall.
The writing hasn’t aged — it’s matured into satire that feels even sharper today.

• I drove aimlessly → the city told stories.
• I followed missions → the characters unraveled.
• I caused chaos → the game smiled and let me.

GTA V Enhanced doesn’t ask you to relearn anything.
It asks you to remember why this worked so well.

It’s still absurd.
Still cynical.
Still confident enough to let you fail loudly.

By the end, Los Santos didn’t feel new.
It felt permanent.

9/10 –
Not because it changed the game,
but because it proved how hard it is to outgrow it.

The only thing "Enhanced" is the connectivity issues and bugs. Obviously, it's GTA V, so [i]obviously[/i] I recommend the game itself. I just won't entertain the "Enhanced" version with a good review.

[b][u]Enhanced Pros:[/u][/b]
- [b]Faster offline loading times[/b]
- [b]Animals in Online[/b]

[b][u]Cons:[/u][/b]
- [b]Slow transactions[/b]: Every 5 transactions, whether that be buying a car or picking up money from the ground puts you on a 1 minute transaction loop. This feels like the equivalent of getting an unskippable ad when watching a video.
- [b]Robbed by Rockstar[/b]: Sometimes R* likes to do this really funny and epic prank where, when you purchase supplies, they will tell you "Unable to purchase supplies at this time" and then just take your money anyway. Or that cute little moment they have when you finish a sell mission, and they decide to forget that you successfully delivered everything and then only give you half the money because they thought you only did half the deliveries.
[b]Now this is NOT an exaggeration. I have so far had to claim back $5,000,000 from R* Support due to this garbage, which they would charge YOU around £40 for in Shark Cards.[/b]
- [b]Buggy Heists[/b]: Another sweet little "feature" R* has is sometimes when their North Sentinel Island servers have a slight little oopsie and you get disconnected from a heist, they'll decide to completely change how you set up the heist and lock you into a set up you never picked with the lowest possible reward (Casino Heist). 
- [b]Wastes Your Time[/b]: Now, as you know, R* already realises your time means nothing to them. They want nothing more than to waste your time. But this is further [i]enhanced[/i] in the "enhanced" version, with around 1 in 10 of your MC Sales being unpaid. So next time you start a sell mission on your own and spend 40 minutes doing the most mundane task of your life, keep in mind that you might not even get paid for it. How cool is that?
- [b]No Text Chat[/b]: Why? Because having people communicate during missions would make the game playable. R* doesn't like that. So they removed it.
- [b]North Korean Voice Chat Monitoring[/b]: If you even so much as breathe the wrong way with Voice Chat active, prepare for the world's most unintelligent artificial intelligence to ban you. Again, they don't want players communicating with each other, that will be bad for business. Players might band together and make money WITHOUT Shark Cards. R* can't have that happen now can they?

Please keep in mind that when I refer to R*, I'm referring to the absolute clowns that they've put in charge of GTA Online. GTA V itself is an INCREDIBLE game as we all very well know. And so are the rest of their games. But there's one department out there that seems like it's filled by people who just figured out how to print "Hello World." Not to mention that they appear to be running servers from 10,000 BCE. 

Also, before someone says "Improved Graphics", don't. They have a Ray Tracing option that doesn't even work.

GTA V - 10/10
GTA V Enhanced - 5/10
Make sure you've saved up all your patience for this one.

Please Note: You'll notice I will continue to play this. But please be aware that I'm merely being an absolute hero by putting up with all of the aforementioned cons. Not to mention keeping R* Support busy with my occasional "You owe me $1,000,000 due to lost money" tickets.

First playthrough review time.

The PC version of GTA V is very well made and runs smoothly. I played the enhanced version, which seems better optimized than the base version with enhanced graphics. The game works well even on older hardware, and most settings can be set to high without major problems. It supports both first and third person views, and switching between them works well. The game is large, so preloading it or installing it on an SSD helps reduce long loading times, especially in online mode. Overall, the performance and graphics make the experience on PC impressive.

The single player mode is well designed, with a world that feels alive and detailed, and I finally completed the whole franchise. I played GTA V many years ago, maybe around 10 years back, but I hadn’t finished it at that time. The story allows switching between multiple characters, which adds variety compared to older games in the series. The game world is seamless, with no invisible walls or constant loading screens while exploring. The controls work best with a controller, especially for driving, and while keyboard and mouse options can be fully customized, I play all games using keyboard and mouse only, even though I have an Xbox controller, because I prefer this input.

I have completed GTA V 100%, including all content, as well as every GTA game from Vice City to GTA 4 Complete Edition. However, since my main focus is on competitive esports FPS games, I don’t aim to 100% complete every single-player game. I bought GTA V mainly for the single player experience and haven't played much online.

Overall, the PC version is polished and well executed. The single player story and the seamless open world demonstrate the continued quality and depth of the game, even years after its release.

I implore you to heed my words and DO NOT buy this game, if you want to enjoy the game please play on a console. Firstly, I am good at the game, not a PRO but still actually put effort into learning game mechanics and trying to better myself and have done so since FIFA 13 UT.

1. Cheaters. This game is FILLED to the brim with cheaters and you might think I am exaggerating / tilted but I promise you, its really THAT bad. It's extremely common in high divisions / champs to have 10+ of your 15 games be either the click script hack (changing slider values to make you slow etc, you'll hear an audible GUI sound when they do it), people using AI to play for them, console players using a Cronus Zen (script cheats), controllers being forcefully disconnected and finally if you're (un)lucky cheaters that replace your ENTIRE team with fake players that cannot be switched to / moved. Oh yeah, did I also mention that cheaters can also fake / spoof being a console to get around users that have crossplay disabled, also for more context I peaked at mid division 3 and played champs and this was my average experience for about the month and a half I played. (I literally couldn't get any higher due to cheaters every game)
EDIT: Forgot to mention that the game has an INVASIVE kernal-level anti cheat that clearly just is false advertising / just doesn't actually exist.

2. The PC version of FC26 is TERRIBLE. Yes, somehow the game being terribly optimized is only the second biggest thing wrong with the game. I cannot speak for mid / entry level PCS but FPS wise my high end PC actually got acceptable FPS without any upscalers and graphics wise it actually looks pretty good on max settings. BUT, and this is a big but, if you want to play ONLINE in friendlies, rivals, champs, clubs etc you have to turn all of your settings to LOW and cap your FPS to either 60 / 120 fps (sigh) or somehow you'll have an extra 3-5ms of input lag on everything you do, for whatever reason this only applies to online modes and works perfectly fine in anything thats offline (squad battles, manager / career mode etc). If you look up input lag FC26 PC you'll find 100's of posts on EA's own forums talking about this exact issue and begging EA to fix it since its been in the game since launch, but alas its still a major problem. (The only things that help are what I said above^)
EDIT: if you also have an Nvidia GPU you need to roll-back to minimum ver. 566.36 any latest driver version will also cause high input lag somehow? The game also has crashing issues if you play uncapped FPS. 

3. Gameplay. Playstyles "in theory" sound like a really cool addition making in-game players more akin to their IRL counterparts with each players unique style and philosophy on how they approach the game, but being classic EA some of the styles are so OVERPOWERED its unreal and have not / WILL not ever be nerfed until the next game comes along. Anticipate+, Finesse+, Low driven+, pinged pass+ tiki taka+ etc... are so strong that actual stats on cards seem to be an afterthought when trying to create meta teams now. AI defending is WAY too strong that people will not even switch too defenders anymore and will just run back with a midfielder because the AI is guaranteed to turn into prime Maldini and block / intercept ANYTHING. (They did a patch recently attempting to nerf it but its still just as OP.) Goalkeepers are either insane or useless, you'll load into a game and you / your opponent will either have a FIFA 14 TOTY Neuer in goal not letting a SINGLE thing go in or you'll have a random bronze keeper that won't even attempt to dive or stop anything, I have scored goals PASSING the ball to the keeper rather then shooting. The bounce backs. HOLY THE BOUNCE BACKS 70% of the time you make a successful tackle the ball will just rebound back to the opponent or just fly across the map 30mph and probably still rebound back to the there defenders.

TLDR; If you really, really want to play FC26 or any future games, please just buy the game on console and turn off crossplay. You will still get cheaters BUT it will be FAR, far less then what's over here on PC. I played on both the ps5 / xbox series X versions respectively and had a much more enjoyable time and encountered only a handful of cheaters + none of the awful input lag that's in online games.

This game is unable to create a shader file in Documents and due to this its locking my FPS to 7 as Ryzen 6000 series processors runs on 2 types of cores i.e. P-core(performance core) , E-core( Efficiency core).

When I researched about it I've come to a realisation that its anti cheat is interfering with the processors by watching CPU threads movement across P/E cores(performance /Efficiency cores) and activates a fail safe that makes the game not save the shaders and drop and lock to 7 FPS

So basically, the root cause is the CPU scheduler conflict on Ryzen 7 6800H Laptops
-> fc 26 + anti cheat detects thread movement between P-cores and E-cores
->Anti-Cheat enters failsafe mode, locking FPS to ~7, even though GPU is fully used
-> windows tweaks , shader cache, or reinstall cannot fix the underlying scheduler conflict

FC 26 is a bold experiment in redefining what football means. 

Passing is optional and completely broken. You press pass, something happens, and you’re left to interpret the result like modern art. Was that a through ball? A clearance? A quiet cry for help from the physics engine? Hard to say, but it’s rarely accurate, and never what you intended. 

Your players actively avoid useful positions. There’s something almost artistic about watching them hide behind defenders or sprint into the same five square meters like it’s a team-building exercise. To be fair, this does add a certain difficulty curve. Just not the fun kind. On a casual level, it’s less "pick up and play" and more “pick up and question your life choices.” You’re not battling the opponent so much as negotiating with your own team, hoping that at least two of them will behave like professional footballers for a few seconds in a row. 

Overall, FC 26 is perfect if you enjoy unpredictability, chaos, and shouting “why are you THERE?” at your screen. If you’re looking for responsive passing, intelligent positioning, or anything resembling tactical awareness, consider it an opportunity to practice patience instead. Lots and lots of patience.

FC 26 is a bold experiment in redefining what football means. 

Passing is optional and completely broken. You press pass, something happens, and you’re left to interpret the result like modern art. Was that a through ball? A clearance? A quiet cry for help from the physics engine? Hard to say, but it’s rarely accurate, and never what you intended. 

Your players actively avoid useful positions. There’s something almost artistic about watching them hide behind defenders or sprint into the same five square meters like it’s a team-building exercise. To be fair, this does add a certain difficulty curve. Just not the fun kind. On a casual level, it’s less "pick up and play" and more “pick up and question your life choices.” You’re not battling the opponent so much as negotiating with your own team, hoping that at least two of them will behave like professional footballers for a few seconds in a row. 

Overall, FC 26 is perfect if you enjoy unpredictability, chaos, and shouting “why are you THERE?” at your screen. If you’re looking for responsive passing, intelligent positioning, or anything resembling tactical awareness, consider it an opportunity to practice patience instead. Lots and lots of patience.

I’ve owned every FIFA game from ’97 to ’21. After stepping away from consoles for a few years, I built a PC and picked up FC26.

I was expecting a much bigger leap from FIFA 21. Mechanically, it still feels almost identical — and honestly, even FIFA 21 didn’t feel that different from 18 or 19. The core gameplay hasn’t really evolved in any meaningful way.

Manager Mode is in the same boat. There are a few tweaks here and there, but nothing that fundamentally changes how it plays. It still feels like the same mode I’ve been playing for years, just with some new menus and minor adjustments.

The graphics are definitely nicer, but even that jump wasn’t as dramatic as I expected going from FIFA 21 on an old Xbox to FC26 on a high‑end gaming PC.

Summary:
In the end, even though so much of it feels familiar, I still find myself recommending FC26. The gameplay is smooth, the matches are genuinely fun, and there’s an undeniable charm to the formula—even if it hasn’t changed much in years. Sure, the focus has clearly shifted toward Ultimate Team lately, mostly for financial reasons, but there’s still plenty of enjoyment to be had outside of that mode. If you’re coming back after a break or just want a solid football game to sink time into, it still delivers where it counts.

There is sadly no competition on the football game market.

FC 26 – 3/10 – Fun Game, But Unplayable on Steam Due to Constant Crashes

FC 26 had all the makings of a solid, fun football game. The gameplay is engaging, with fluid mechanics and a satisfying level of control over your team. The matches are intense, the player movements are smooth, and the action feels just right when it works. For a moment, it seems like the perfect pick for casual football fans or those looking for a quick but enjoyable gaming experience. Unfortunately, that's where the praise ends—because the game simply doesn’t work properly on Steam.

The major issue with FC 26 is its stability. Despite the fun gameplay on offer, the game crashes frequently, making it nearly impossible to get through a full match or enjoy any extended sessions. Whether it's a random freeze mid-game, crashing to the desktop after loading a match, or losing progress after an unexpected shutdown, the game’s technical issues ruin what could have been an otherwise enjoyable experience. At this point, FC 26 feels like it’s been released in an unfinished state on Steam, with no clear fixes in sight.

When it does work, the game is fun. The mechanics are solid, the visuals are decent (if not groundbreaking), and the sound design—while nothing special—provides a good atmosphere during matches. There’s a satisfying sense of progression, team management, and strategy that could keep you invested for hours. If the game ran smoothly, it’d be a decent football sim. However, these positives are completely overshadowed by the constant crashes that prevent any meaningful progress.

The fact that FC 26 is unplayable on Steam is a huge issue, and it’s disappointing because the game has potential. For players who are able to get through a match without it crashing, there’s a solid experience waiting for them, but that’s a big “if.” The lack of a reliable experience on such a major platform makes it hard to recommend.

If you’re still determined to play it, I highly suggest buying it through the EA App instead. It seems to be more stable there, and you’ll actually be able to enjoy the game without the constant crashing and frustration that comes with the Steam version.

FC 26 3/10 – A Fun Game, If You Can Actually Play It
FC 26 could have been a solid sports title, but the constant crashing makes it unplayable for most players on Steam. The potential is there, but it’s buried under a mountain of technical issues. Until the developers address the stability problems, this game is more frustrating than fun. If you're looking for a working football game, you’re better off buying it on the EA App, where the experience is at least more reliable.

Having played FIFA games since FIFA 13, I'll admit the gameplay does take some getting used to. I was initially appalled at the how clumsy and unresponsive the players felt, but IMO it's more realistic after getting used to the game. The animations are poor, as evidenced by watching some goal instant replays and seeing collision physics poorly integrated with balls going through people's legs and body parts morphing together. It's a true shame how inconsistent it really is. 
Furthermore, having played mostly Player Career mode in every FIFA game I played, I can say this is an extremely disappointing showing from EA FC 26. Going back to FIFA 17 and seeing how much effort they put into The Journey, allowing you to truly immerse yourself into a story was fantastic. It's saddening to see their pure focus on Ultimate Team and the lack of effort that results in other gameplay modes. 
Finally, it's just too easy to progress both in UT and Career Mode. In previous games, you would start UT with a bronze squad and celebrate when you finally could afford your first gold player. An 80 rated squad was something that took genuine effort, where now you are gifted 90 OVR players from the moment you start the game. In Player Career, you used to start out as a 65 OVR and be sent on loan to third division teams to prove your worth. You would have to genuinely grind and immerse yourself in the game to succeed, and now none of that exists. 
Overall, its fun to play as an arcade game, but as the number one Football video game on the market, it is extremely flawed.

FC 26 – 3/10 – Fun Game, But Unplayable on Steam Due to Constant Crashes

FC 26 had all the makings of a solid, fun football game. The gameplay is engaging, with fluid mechanics and a satisfying level of control over your team. The matches are intense, the player movements are smooth, and the action feels just right when it works. For a moment, it seems like the perfect pick for casual football fans or those looking for a quick but enjoyable gaming experience. Unfortunately, that's where the praise ends—because the game simply doesn’t work properly on Steam.

The major issue with FC 26 is its stability. Despite the fun gameplay on offer, the game crashes frequently, making it nearly impossible to get through a full match or enjoy any extended sessions. Whether it's a random freeze mid-game, crashing to the desktop after loading a match, or losing progress after an unexpected shutdown, the game’s technical issues ruin what could have been an otherwise enjoyable experience. At this point, FC 26 feels like it’s been released in an unfinished state on Steam, with no clear fixes in sight.

When it does work, the game is fun. The mechanics are solid, the visuals are decent (if not groundbreaking), and the sound design—while nothing special—provides a good atmosphere during matches. There’s a satisfying sense of progression, team management, and strategy that could keep you invested for hours. If the game ran smoothly, it’d be a decent football sim. However, these positives are completely overshadowed by the constant crashes that prevent any meaningful progress.

The fact that FC 26 is unplayable on Steam is a huge issue, and it’s disappointing because the game has potential. For players who are able to get through a match without it crashing, there’s a solid experience waiting for them, but that’s a big “if.” The lack of a reliable experience on such a major platform makes it hard to recommend.

If you’re still determined to play it, I highly suggest buying it through the EA App instead. It seems to be more stable there, and you’ll actually be able to enjoy the game without the constant crashing and frustration that comes with the Steam version.

FC 26 3/10 – A Fun Game, If You Can Actually Play It
FC 26 could have been a solid sports title, but the constant crashing makes it unplayable for most players on Steam. The potential is there, but it’s buried under a mountain of technical issues. Until the developers address the stability problems, this game is more frustrating than fun. If you're looking for a working football game, you’re better off buying it on the EA App, where the experience is at least more reliable.

Having played FIFA games since FIFA 13, I'll admit the gameplay does take some getting used to. I was initially appalled at the how clumsy and unresponsive the players felt, but IMO it's more realistic after getting used to the game. Additionally, I will give credit to some of the details of Manager Mode and Player Career Mode. 
However, this is one of the least optimized games I have ever played. The number of random disconnects, server timeouts, and random bugs I encounter in this game would make me believe this was an early access beta. The animations are poor, as evidenced by watching some goal instant replays and seeing collision physics poorly integrated with balls going through people's legs and body parts morphing together. It's a true shame how inconsistent it really is. 
Furthermore, having played mostly Player Career mode in every FIFA game I played, I can say this is an extremely disappointing showing from EA FC 26. Going back to FIFA 17 and seeing how much effort they put into The Journey, allowing you to truly immerse yourself into a story was fantastic. It's saddening to see their pure focus on Ultimate Team and the lack of effort that results in other gameplay modes. 
Finally, it's just too easy to progress both in UT and Career Mode. In previous games, you would start UT with a bronze squad and celebrate when you finally could afford your first gold player. An 80 rated squad was something that took genuine effort, where now you are gifted 90 OVR players from the moment you start the game. In Player Career, you used to start out as a 65 OVR and be sent on loan to third division teams to prove your worth. You would have to genuinely grind and immerse yourself in the game to succeed, and now none of that exists. 
Overall, its fun to play as an arcade game, but as the number one Football video game on the market, it is extremely flawed.

I went into EA Sports FC 26 hoping it would pull me back in, especially since I hadn’t played this style of football game in several years. Unfortunately, I got bored far quicker than expected.

For context, I have been playing Football Manager, so it’s not like I’m disconnected from football games entirely. That might actually be part of the problem. After spending time with a game that offers depth, strategy, and long-term engagement, EA Sports FC 26 felt shallow by comparison. Even allowing for the fact that they’re very different types of games, FC 26 just didn’t give me much reason to stay invested.

The core gameplay loop started to feel repetitive almost immediately. Matches blended together, and despite waiting for something to hook me — a new mechanic, a sense of progression, or even just that “one more match” feeling — it never really arrived. As background, my experience with FIFA and the like is that I jumped from FIFA 2006 to EA FC 24 and then to EA FC 26. FC 26 suffers from a lot of the same problems as EA FC 24, namely several glaring glitches that make the game incredibly frustrating to play. For instance, the game will randomly experience a catastrophic drop in frame rate making a match practically unplayable. This is especially infuriating in a squad battle or rivals game where you really need the game to perform reliably. I've experienced instances where my custom control settings get corrupted where certain actions simply don't work, like clicking R3 to flick the ball up. Other weird glitches that have not been fixed since FC 24 include  "recommended" graphic settings producing low frame rates, drop down menus of players that have been changed out not disappearing when you start entering the late phases of a match, odd hair color glitches where player and fan models have neon hair colors, and ultimate team games just disconnecting and you being given a loss for the disconnection. A problem unique to FC 26 is the likely AI generated crowd models repeating themselves where you see twins or triplets of different people in the crowds.

         I have yet to take a look at the player career mode for this game (once I do might revisit this review), but I recall FC 24 suffering from the problem of an incredibly boring investment system that had you wasting money on such things as "buy a yacht" and having a lackluster personality system that locked you out of different abilities because you couldn't go back an reallocate points to unlock them. I honestly don't have much faith that things have changed, but again I will return to this review if they have.

         I've played a lot of FC 24 and 26 because I enjoy football. But spending any of your gameplay time mindlessly opening card packs that give you a less than 1% chance to get good quality players, dealing with unacceptable glitches, and a steep learning curve that isn't intuitive to new members of the community make it extremely difficult to recommend this game in good faith. A game series that has been in existence for this long does not have any excuse for being so hostile to the player in its design plagued by negligence and lack of care. The tag line "EA finally listened" should not be a point of pride attached to this game. Instead, fans should take it as damning evidence that this company believes that the bare minimum of listening to the fan base's criticism and feedback is too high a bar for them on a normal day when it is in fact the lowest hanging fruit in the gaming industry.

          FC represents a lot of the worst of what gaming has to offer. I can only hope that they one day gain the wisdom that a game should not be a yearly release if it means putting out a low quality product. But history has shown that having faith in EA is guaranteed to be met with disappointment.

This gaming franchise has gone from by far the best football/soccer video gaming experience to absolute garbage. It's really sad to say having played FIFA since 09 and FUT since 11. The Devs really got my hopes up at the beginning of the game cycle because they were "listening to community feedback." However, as soon as the pro players and everyone who is willing to buy FIFA points complained, they reverted back and completely forgot what they were going differently than the past couple of years.

The game play has gotten so unrealistic and the game holds your hand so much with the AI defending. All of the broken mechanics in this game make it so hard to play and enjoy anymore. I know making a video game realistic especially when it comes to an actual sport because there is so many unpredictable variables, but its like they didn't even try. They just slap on the same name and change the number every year but change nothing with the actual gameplay or mechanics. And don't even get me started on the stupid playstyles. They have completely ruined cards. I remember when getting a card that had all 80s stats meant something, now just need a bronze card with Finesse+ and you can score from anywhere. Playstyles have been the worst addition in recent years. And the power curve still didn't change, like they said it would.

Some ideas that they NEED to do in order to make this game enjoyable again would be:

1. REMOVE playstyles and roles completely (My 90+ CM that has 90+ Passing should be able to make a 10 yard pass, just because they don't have Tiki Taka doesn't mean that their passing stats are irrelevant)
2. Actually make the power curve slower (We don't need a promo every single week, promos are actually killing the game, there are way too many cards in this game anymore. There should only be a handful of promos every game cycle. TOTY, TOTS, TOTT, FS, RTTK, and FUTTIES. TOTW, MOTM, and POTM cards are also completely fine. EVOs, are enough already on top of the millions of other cards that we get, we sill see the same 20 players on everyone's teams already. The only reason as to why we have so many promos is so that they can keep cleaning out everyone's wallets, it's actually so pathetic)
3. Make the gameplay feel responsive and fun again (I'm no coder or software engineer, however, for all the money that this company has, it's mind-blowing as to how this game can never have something that absolutely breaks the game and doesn't ruin it. Every update they "fix" something, but then make the gameplay worse and add two more broken mechanics and then we don't get a patch for 2 months. There are SO many other studios and developers that have WAY LESS people and WAY LESS money and make a better game all round)
4. Bring back the old reward system from champs (make rewards come out on Thursdays again instead of instant gratification, this actually gave you something to look forward to instead of people going out and finishing their champs games and flooding the market, the market is already ruined. Plus when the rewards were on Thursdays, you probably thought you had a terrible weekend league, couple days do bye and now you get your rewards, look you get something good out of them)
5. Balance the Men and Women competing against each other (I'm all for having the women in the game. It adds to much more to the game. However, when comparing stats between the men and women, some stats make absolutely no sense at all. I think that they should have 3 versions for all game modes to compensate for this. I mean, they should have an all men's, all women's, and a combined men's and women's game modes for each of champs, rivals, and squad battles. And yes, I understand that when women were introduced into FIFA several years ago, it was only in kick off, and not many people played that. But, Pina should never be bodying VVD and Rio, that just would never happen IRL)
6. Stop trying to make this an E-Sports game (the gameplay is way too unpredictable to be considered an E-Sports game. You have to have certain that when you take a shot on goal from 10 yards out that it's going to go into the same sport 100 times out of 100. If not then stop and figure out which route you want to take with this game. Either E-Sports or for the casual football/soccer fans)

If they really want to bring bad the joy of this game instead of catering towards E-Sports and the rich, they really need to take a step back and make some changes going forward. Like I said I have been playing this game for over 10 years, but certain decisions have seriously hurt this game. Because I know how good this game could be and it's so frustrating to see and play anymore. So, if you are thinking of getting this game, as of right now, DON'T! Save your money and find something else that can make you feel the same fun and enjoyment. Since video games are supposed to be played for fun and relaxation!
